summary: Designed the consent-gated git push mechanism across all three absorbed phases (grant token + /please mint hook + guards + tests; /please command + docs sweep; orchestrator dispatch relay). Confirmed the prohibition is currently rule-text-only with zero mechanical enforcement. Settled the grant-scope/invalidation predicate, the categorical exclusions (force-push and master pushes stay outside any grant), that PR/MR creation and /merge stay fully user-only, the audit-event design, and the .decisions.json replay-hazard closure (a YES never mints a grant directly). Surfaced two findings not named in the dispatch: (1) root-files/settings.json and merge-sources/settings-hooks.json reach different consumer populations, and guard-destructive-git.sh's own Bash-matcher registration is missing from the latter -- a live latent propagation gap the new hooks must not repeat; (2) commands/README.md has no per-command table, so the absorbed task's 'add a row there' instruction needs correction.

artifacts.summary: Full design research covering grant semantics, integrity/mint-path, hook registration mechanics, categorical exclusions, audit-event design, and the orchestrator dispatch-relay path for consent-gated git push across all three absorbed implementation phases.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's agent-system source store, root-files/settings.json (install-once template, only reaches a repo whose .claude/settings.json does not yet exist) and merge-sources/settings-hooks.json (add-only deep-merge fragment, the only path that reaches an already-initialized consumer repo) are NOT interchangeable hook-registration targets. Any new PreToolUse/UserPromptSubmit/etc. hook must be registered in BOTH, each as its own dedicated single-command matcher object (never appended into an existing shared matcher's hooks array, which breaks vim.deep_equal-based re-merge idempotency). Cross-checking the two files against each other is the only way to catch a hook that reaches fresh deploys but never propagates to existing ones -- guard-destructive-git.sh's own Bash-matcher entry is a live example of this exact gap (present in root-files/settings.json, absent from merge-sources/settings-hooks.json).

For a Claude Code UserPromptSubmit hook: the .prompt field on stdin JSON carries the LITERAL, unexpanded text the user typed, not an expanded slash-command's markdown file content -- confirmed indirectly via hooks/wezterm-task-number.sh, which pattern-matches literal '/research', '/plan' etc. prefixes directly against .prompt (only correct if unexpanded). This makes UserPromptSubmit a viable tamper-resistant mint point for a human-consent gate, since a dispatched subagent has no independent prompt-submission lifecycle and therefore cannot trigger it -- but that non-triggering property should be empirically verified (temporary logging + a subagent dispatch starting with the trigger text) before being relied on for a security-critical design, not merely inferred from architecture.

In this repo, a model's file-mutation channels are exactly Claude Code's own tool-call surface (Bash, Write, Edit, plus any write-capable MCP tool a given deploy has wired) -- every one of those is interceptable by a PreToolUse hook returning exit 2. So a PreToolUse guard blocking writes to a specific path (mirroring guard-destructive-git.sh's quote-stripped COMMAND_SCAN pattern-matching technique for Bash, plus a Write|Edit matcher for the dedicated tools) genuinely closes the model's write channel to that path completely -- PROVIDED the guard's matcher list covers every write-capable tool currently active in that deploy. This is a real, load-bearing scope qualification for any 'model cannot forge file X' design: state explicitly which matchers the guard covers and note that a newly-wired write-capable tool (e.g. a future MCP filesystem-write server) requires revisiting the guard's matcher list, rather than assuming Bash|Write|Edit is exhaustive forever.
